title: Complement of market surge
scenario_markdown: An economic forecasting model estimates a 35% probability ($P(A) = 0.35$) that the market will surge in the upcoming quarter. Find the probability that the market does NOT experience a surge ($P(A^c)$).
assumptions: Valid probability space with sample space S
Surge and non-surge partition the sample space: A union A^c = S and A cap A^c = empty

approval.notes: Reviewed derivation: P(A^c) = 1 - P(A) = 1 - 0.35 = 0.65. Verified partition axiom.

stages.prompt_markdown: Which fundamental probability rule relates an event $A$ to its complement $A^c$?

options.text_markdown: $P(A^c) = 1 - P(A)$ because an event and its complement partition the sample space

options.hint_markdown: Probability cannot exceed one. If P(A)=0.35, 1/0.35 > 1.
Probabilities must always be non-negative numbers in [0, 1].

stages.explanation_markdown: By the complement axiom, $P(A) + P(A^c) = P(S) = 1$, which gives $P(A^c) = 1 - P(A)$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate $P(A^c) = 1 - 0.35$. Enter as a decimal, percent, or fraction.
